criteria.no: The compliance claim is asserted without anything checkable, or no compliance claim is made.
criteria.unclear: Something that might be evidence is mentioned, but it is not clear that it supports the compliance claim.
criteria.yes: The description points to at least one checkable artifact (path, diff, command, test, comparison) that supports the compliance claim.

evidenced.instructions: Where `item.text` claims the directive in `anchor.statement` was followed, does it cite concrete, checkable evidence for that claim: file paths, commit or diff references, commands that were run, test names or output, or a comparison against the required source? A bare assertion such as 'we followed the anchor' or 'based on X' with nothing checkable does not count. If the description does not claim the directive was followed at all, answer no.

criteria.no: The description is silent about the directive, or says it was deferred, skipped, or left for later.
criteria.unclear: The description mentions the directive's topic but it is not possible to tell whether the directive was followed.
criteria.yes: The description states that the work did what the directive requires, with the directive's specific content present.

implemented.instructions: According to `item.text`, was the directive in `anchor.statement` followed in what was actually built? Look for the directive's specific content in the account of the work: the required starting point was used, the required method was applied, the constraint was kept. A statement of intent or a plan to do it later does not count as followed. Judge whether the account says the directive was followed, not whether the account proves it.

criteria.no: The work is in a different part of the system or a different activity, and it could neither follow nor break the anchor.
criteria.unclear: The description is too vague to tell what the work touched.
criteria.yes: The work changed, created, removed, or depends on the thing the anchor statement is about.

relevant.instructions: The state holds a description of delivered work (`item.title`, `item.text`) and one anchor: a directive the user stated verbatim in `anchor.statement`, with the area it governs in `anchor.scope`. Does the delivered work described in `item.text` touch the subject that `anchor.statement` talks about? Judge overlap of subject matter only. Do not judge compliance.

criteria.no: Nothing in the description conflicts with the directive, whether or not the directive is mentioned.
criteria.unclear: The description is ambiguous enough that the work might or might not conflict with the directive.
criteria.yes: The description states an action, approach, or decision in the delivered work that cannot be reconciled with the directive.

violated.instructions: Does `item.text` show that the work did something `anchor.statement` rules out, or used a different approach than the one `anchor.statement` requires? Examples: the anchor says to start from an existing implementation and the work was written from scratch; the anchor forbids a dependency and the work added it; the anchor fixes a boundary and the work crossed it. Silence about the directive is not a violation. Judge conflict only.

criteria.no: It makes no compliance claim, or only asserts compliance without a checkable citation.
criteria.unclear: An apparent citation exists but its support for the claimed limit is unclear.
criteria.yes: It cites a path, test, command, diff, commit or comparison supporting the delivered repository-level limit.

evidenced.instructions: If `item.text` claims that the delivered scheduler keeps at most one built-in beads-cache bd sync row per repository, does it cite a concrete checkable artifact supporting that claim? Judge citation support only; silence and a bare assertion do not count.

criteria.no: It says the limit was not kept, only plans it, or makes no claim that it was kept.
criteria.unclear: It mentions the built-in limit but leaves the delivered cardinality uncertain.
criteria.yes: It says the delivered scheduler limits each repository to zero or one built-in sync row or refuses a second such row.

implemented.instructions: Does `item.text` state that the delivered work kept at most one built-in beads-cache bd sync schedule row for each repository? Judge the claimed delivered restriction only; silence, future intent, and discussion of scheduling alone do not state that it was kept.

criteria.no: It concerns an activity that cannot affect or describe sync schedule rows.
criteria.unclear: Its subject is too vague to tell whether it touches sync schedule rows.
criteria.yes: It handles sync schedule rows or their repository-level management.

relevant.instructions: Does the delivered work in `item.text` touch creating, storing, editing, refusing, deleting, or managing built-in beads-cache bd sync schedule rows per repository in sc-cron? Judge subject overlap only. Silence about compliance is not a conflict judgment.

criteria.no: No described delivered behavior exceeds one built-in sync row per repository; omission alone is no conflict.
criteria.unclear: A described cardinality is genuinely ambiguous between an allowed and a forbidden value.
criteria.yes: The delivered behavior permits multiple built-in sync rows within one repository, including one per scope in that repository.

violated.instructions: Does `item.text` describe delivered behavior allowing more than one built-in beads-cache bd sync schedule row in any one repository? Custom non-built-in jobs and a single built-in row in each of several repositories are allowed by the authority. Silence about the limit is not a breach.

criteria.no: No compliance claim is made or no checkable supporting artifact is named.
criteria.unclear: Something resembling evidence is named but its relation to the claim cannot be determined.
criteria.yes: A named test, path, command, diff, commit, result or comparison supports the claim that a second built-in sync row is refused.

evidenced.instructions: Is the delivered repository-level built-in sync limit claimed in `item.text` backed there by at least one identifiable supporting artifact? Do not independently execute the artifact. A citation demonstrating a breach is not support for compliance.

criteria.no: The account reports a breach, deferral, future proposal, or no delivered enforcement claim.
criteria.unclear: The account concerns that restriction but cannot say whether delivered behavior enforced it.
criteria.yes: The account says the delivered behavior enforces that repository-level maximum.

implemented.instructions: According to the account in `item.text`, was the ANC-008 repository-level maximum of one built-in beads-cache bd sync schedule row preserved in the built scheduler? Evaluate the account of completion, without requiring proof or inferring completion from silence.

criteria.no: The work is unrelated to schedule rows and cannot affect them.
criteria.unclear: The description does not identify enough subject matter to determine overlap.
criteria.yes: The work operates on, documents, or depends on the relevant schedule rows.

relevant.instructions: Is repository-level built-in beads-cache sync scheduling part of the work described in `item.text`, as governed by `anchor.scope`? Decide overlap only, including changes to general schedule-row management; do not decide whether the limit was kept.

criteria.no: There is no stated breach, including silence or allowed custom jobs and separate repositories.
criteria.unclear: The stated action is too ambiguous to determine whether it permits a second built-in sync row in one repository.
criteria.yes: A stated action breaks the one-built-in-sync-row-per-repository restriction.

violated.instructions: Can the delivered action stated in `item.text` be reconciled with ANC-008, which prohibits a second built-in beads-cache sync row for the same repository? Judge conflict only, not whether compliance was asserted or evidenced.
